📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 13:05, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 13:05.

Liverpool are reportedly keeping a close eye on Borussia Dortmund youngster Joane Gadou.

The 19-year-old joined the German club in the summer transfer window from Red Bull Salzburg and has already made a strong impression at his new side.

The youngster has made 10 Bundesliga appearances, starting nine of them, while also featuring five times in the Champions League.

According to CaughtOffside's The Daily Briefing, Liverpool are among the clubs showing keen interest in the young centre-back, who is also capable of operating at right-back.

The Reds could face competition from Manchester United and Arsenal for Gadou, while Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain are also monitoring his progress.

Gadou is particularly strong in the air and has already produced several eye-catching performances, with his display in the 1-1 draw against Arsenal attracting considerable attention.

The report claims that although several top clubs are keeping a close watch on his development, none are presently ready to make a move for him.

The Frenchman is under contract at Dortmund until 2031, and while a departure could become a possibility at some point in the future, a move is not expected in the immediate term.

Liverpool will probably need to sign a upcoming centre-back next summer, with Joe Gomez potentially heading for the exit.

With Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni, the Reds already have two highly talented young centre-backs, and there would be little harm in further strengthening their pool of promising defensive prospects.

Virgil van Dijk has been outstanding once again this season and is showing few signs that age is beginning to catch up with him.

Liverpool should certainly continue monitoring Gadou's progress for the remainder of the campaign, and if an opportunity arises, taking a chance on him as a potential long-term replacement for Gomez could prove worthwhile.

  • Now, Pete O’Rourke states on X that Russell’s performances have drawn interest at a higher level with a number of unnamed League One teams interested in a potential winter move.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, crawley Town signed Jonny Russell from Northern Irish outfit Glentoran in January, and he has been a bright spark in their tough start to the season. The Red Devils are presently rooted to the foot of the League Two table, but the 22-year-old has impressed.

Now, Pete O’Rourke states on X that Russell’s performances have drawn interest at a higher level with a number of unnamed League One teams interested in a potential winter move.

Industry observers note that the Northern Ireland U21 international has been deployed at both centre-back and left-back this term with Kevin Blackwell’s arrival resulting in his upturn in form. Russell has been integral to Town’s defensive improvements, helping secure their first clean sheets of the season against Oldham Athletic and Barnet as the club aim to avoid relegation to non-league for the first time since 2011.

Russell was a relatively unknown quantity when he touched down in West Sussex at the beginning of the year. The move brought an end to his 11-year association with boyhood club Glentoran as he headed to the League Two strugglers.

The move was a gamble for Russell given his settled position in Glentoran’s side and Crawley Town’s precarious position towards the bottom of the table. However, the switch has ultimately paid off for all parties.

He played on 19 occasions as the Red Devils avoided the drop. Russell showed signs of inconsistency with a handful of mistakes, something which has been eradicated under Blackwell this term.

Russell has grown into his time with Crawley Town and it’s unsurprising teams higher up the pyramid are starting to take note. The 22-year-old ranks as one of the division’s best defenders with a 100% successful dribble rate and winning 4.76 of his aerial duels per 90 (FotMob).

In a recent development, although Crawley Town have shown encouraging signs of shoring up at the back, with Russell at the heart of that. However, the precarious position they find themselves in could prompt them to cash in on their star defender in January, and he may be tempted by a move as well.

Town reportedly forked out £100,000 for his services, and they will undoubtedly make a profit.

If they were to hold on to Russell until the end of the season in the hope they retain their League Two status, they could risk losing a large sum of money in the summer if they drop down into the National League.

Russell has certainly proven his credentials in a struggling side so he would only benefit from better players around him, with a step-up to League One being the perfect platform to continue his development.

Nonetheless, his impact for Crawley Town cannot be overstated, and losing him in the upcoming transfer window would significantly hamper their survival hopes.

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 17:31 EST, 23 November 2026 | Updated: 04:29 EST, 24 November 2026.

David Moyes’ record-breaking night as Everton manager could not have been more miserable.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record for most games in the dugout.

But that was about the only positive he could take away from the Gtech Community Stadium, as high-flying Brentford battered ten-man Everton on an evening to forget for the 63-year-old Scotsman.

Daily Mail Sport's Bobby Manzi was at the Gtech Community Stadium on a torrid night for the Toffees...

The Bees can mix it with major boys.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

They climbed to sixth, leapfrogging Leeds — who have had far more praise lavished on them this season than Keith Andrews’ reliable side.

Brentford are disciplined with plenty of attacking flair, even with frontman and top goalscorer Igor Thiago suspended.

In his 593rd game as Toffees boss, Moyes broke Harry Catterick’s 75-year record.

Brentford, having missed out on European football on goal difference last season, are showing all the signs of being there or thereabouts again.

The Premier League lacks quality this season, but Brentford are consistent, losing just twice.

This well-oiled Andrews machine must take advantage of the floundering elite, with Manchester United, Chelsea and Tottenham all struggling, and finally secure Europe.

‘We set out this season looking to be better than last season, and if that happens, we will be flying to different destinations next season,’ Andrews said of their European hopes.’.

‘We've got a very competitive squad that strives to get better. If we continue with that mindset, we'll hopefully be in a good place.

‘I enjoyed us,’ he added about the performance. ‘I thought we were very good. We played with real bravery, courage and energy.’.

It has been revealed that brentford limited Everton to just three touches in the penalty area in the first half. They grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck and pinned their opponents back.

In a recent development, jaidon Anthony was superb on the flank, providing two assists. Midfielder Vitaly Janelt capped off a brilliant display with a wonder strike from 25 yards, finding the top corner with his left foot.

It was a surprise to see Kevin Schade benched but this team is so cohesive, with more focus on the unit than any individual stars, that victory was light work for them.

Brentford: Kelleher 7; Kayode 7, Ajer 7, van den Berg 7, Lewis-Potter 9 (Diouf 74min, 6); Yarmolyuk 8 (Jensen 74, 7), Janelt 8 (Sangare 82); Ouattara 6 (Schade 66, 6), Damsgaard 7, Anthony 8 (Carvalho 81, 7); Wilson 7.

Everton: Pickford 5; O’Brien 5, Tarkowski 4, Branthwaite 5, Mykolenko 5; Armstrong 5, Garner 6 (Norgaard 85); Rohl 5 (Keane 69, 6), Dewsbury-Hall 5 (Hackney 69, 6), George 5 (Grealish 66, 5); Barry 4 (Johnson 69, 5).

Sources indicate that both of Keane Lewis-Potter’s goals had an element of fortune attached. But teams earn that luck when they manage ten shots in their opponents’ penalty area in just 45 minutes.

Lewis Potter starred at left-back, registering seven shots — the most of any player — and the joint-most touches in the opposition box. He was a menace and integral to every Brentford attack.

James Tarkowski endured a depressing return to his former club when he was shown the first Premier League red card of his career.

It will split opinion, but in this day and age it is a clear red card. Although the Everton defender won the ball, his studs connected with Yehor Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

The speed and intensity of the tackle endangered his opponent. He had to go.

Referee Craig Pawson brandished a yellow, but a quick trip to the monitor saw it upgraded. Tarkowski ran down the tunnel before Pawson could even get the red card out of his pocket.

The home support enjoyed it, having taunted their former player throughout the first half.

To compound Everton’s misery, the first game of Tarkowski three-match ban is next weekend’s Merseyside derby.

Although Tarkowski won the ball, his studs connected with Yarmolyuk’s shin on follow-through.

It has been revealed that A deflated Moyes had few complaints. ‘My feeling at the time was it wasn’t a red because James easily got to the ball before the Brentford player,’ the Everton boss said.

‘But after I saw it again, Tarky's boot is a bit higher than I'd like, so I can understand why the decision went against us.

It has been revealed that ‘We didn’t play well. Brentford did and credit to them. A bit unfortunate with the goals, it made it look even worse than it was.’.

Everton were unbeaten in four games at Brentford before this and their defeat came in the form of the sublime and the ridiculous.

The first goal was all about Anthony undoing Everton on the left before Lewis-Potter was given far too much space to get his shot away. The deflection was unfortunate, but the defending was poor to begin with.

In a recent development, tarkowski blocked an initial effort from Lewis-Potter for the second goal but the ball fell straight back to him, and Jake O’Brien helped his second attempt past Jordan Pickford. Once again, Everton should have done better and cleared the initial free-kick.

Portuguese forward Fabio Carvalho could not believe his luck when he added a late fourth, tapping in as Mathias Jensen’s corner flew straight past the congested pack at the near post.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.
  • The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the latest City head coach, has landed his number one target.
  • City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have equalled the British record transfer on deadline day after agreeing to pay £125m to sign midfielder Enzo Fernández from Chelsea.

The deal brings to an end the biggest saga of the summer and means that Enzo Maresca, the latest City head coach, has landed his number one target.

City left it until the last day of the transfer window to strike an agreement after Chelsea decided that Fernández’s exit was in the best interests of the club. But a late move to replace the Argentine with Monaco midfielder Lamie Camara collapsed to the anger of the Premier League club, leaving Xabi Alonso one player light among his midfield options.

Having refused to meet Chelsea’s self-imposed deadline to sign Fernández for £120m earlier in the summer, City had to equal the £125m Liverpool paid Newcastle United for Alexander Isak 12 months earlier.

Fernández had made it clear that he wanted to leave Chelsea some time ago and was left out of Alonso’s squad for the victories last week over Luton Town, in the Carabao Cup, and Brighton.

According to recent reports, having initially wanted to join Real Madrid, Fernández set his heart on linking back up with Maresca at City. The pair share a close relationship and had kept in touch after Maresca left Chelsea at the start of the year.

This is the second time Fernández has become the most expensive player in British transfer history, having previously set the record when he joined Chelsea for £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Introducing our fresh Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855.

During his time at Chelsea, 25-year-old Fernández won the Club World Cup and the Europa Conference League but he was also at the centre of controversy.

In January 2025, Fernández posted a video of himself and some of his Argentina international team-mates singing an offensive song about France players of African origin after winning the Copa America. He apologised to his Chelsea team-mates and made a donation to an anti-discrimination charity, but was still made the team’s vice-captain.

Recent findings suggest that last season was Fernández’s best goalscoring campaign, as he netted 15 goals in all competitions for Chelsea but the club finished 10th in the Premier League table. In April, he was suspended for two games by the club for suggesting he would like to live in Madrid – which was perceived as a come and get me plea to Real Madrid.

He angered England fans with his celebration after scoring against Thomas Tuchel’s team in Argentina’s World Cup semi-final victory over England, before being sent-off in the final defeat by Spain.

Chelsea fans booed Fernández in pre-season, although the club’s travelling supporters sang his name when he was introduced as a substitute in the victory over Fulham at the start of this season.

Recent findings suggest that fernández thanked his team-mates and the Chelsea staff in an emotional farewell post on Instagram. He added: “I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven’t been in a good place.

“Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.

Sources indicate that “Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.

Industry observers note that “I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.

Industry observers note that “But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I’ve said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.

According to recent reports, “But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.”.

Proper City 🤩🩵 pic.twitter.com/TfRTZOnPrw.

The sale of Fernández means that Chelsea have set a latest British transfer record of their own, having secured more than £500m in sales and loan fees during the summer transfer window.

Chelsea set about spending some of the money made from the Fernández sale by agreeing a last-minute deal for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara.

Monaco had rejected a bid of £38.5m from Chelsea on deadline day, but an improved offer of £47m was accepted late on Tuesday night, only to be called off by Monaco on the stroke of the 11pm deadline.

Chelsea had been able to complete a medical during negotiations and Camara agreed to a six-year contract with the option of a further year to bolster Alonso’s midfield options, but he will now not join the club.

Chelsea had also seen at least one offer for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott rejected this summer, while the club highlighted an interest in Roma’s Manu Kone and explored whether or not a move for Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi would be possible earlier this month.

Chilly tonight... pic.twitter.com/VihgKCScfn.

The 21-year-old midfielder who came through the ranks at Real Madrid has been signed from Stuttgart.

It has been revealed that brighton’s sporting director Mike Cave said: “We’re delighted to welcome Chema to the club. He has an excellent pedigree having come through at Real Madrid; he followed that with a very good season with Stuttgart last season.

“We had been aware of Chema’s potential for sometime, and we are delighted to welcome him to the club, and look forward to working with him.”.

Fernandez says: “Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times.

“Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.

“I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success.

“If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my newly introduced teammates and become a better player.

Introducing our new Argentinian Blue 🇦🇷🩵 pic.twitter.com/nEHQ1oM855.

Zirkzee is staying at United. No move to Everton. United want the cover in attack and Everton’s approach happened too late with no chance of replacing him.

Crystal Palace have agreed a deal to re-sign Ben Chilwell. The 29-year-old was on loan at Palace last year and deal struck with Strasbourg for him to leave French club and return to the Premier League.

Sunderland were involved in the most bewildering transfer of the summer on deadline day as they fought a day-long tug-of-war with Crystal Palace for winger Malick Fofana.

On a day of claims and counterclaims, Sunderland have finally triumphed in the battle to land the Belgium international just an hour before the deadline.

But despite their success, it was a transfer that will leave a sour taste in the mouth to many, with the player repeatedly changing his mind about which club he wanted to join.

As the saga dragged on, it is understood Fofana had a medical in Lyon with both Sunderland and Crystal Palace given access to the information as he still could not decide which club to join as talks continued into the evening.

Sunderland had a bid of around £25m accepted by Lyon on Tuesday morning and thought they had an agreement with both the player and his agent on personal terms and fees only for Palace to make a late attempt to hijack the deal.

The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, rolled out a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

Sources indicate that after so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

Recent findings suggest that “I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

Sources indicate that “I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”.

Sources indicate that richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”.

It has been revealed that “If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

Recent findings suggest that “But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”.

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

Sources indicate that in an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

It has been revealed that will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

In a recent development, this has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

Recent findings suggest that as reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Industry observers note that spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

It has been revealed that A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

In a recent development, everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A significant year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Sources indicate that good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

In a recent development, enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

Recent findings suggest that A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Industry observers note that newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Industry observers note that barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next major thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

Brentford defender Nathan Collins is reportedly high on Manchester United's list of targets for the January transfer window.

With the side languishing in 19th place in the Premier League table, a major squad overhaul is required in January, although reports suggest Pochettino may not be handed a substantial transfer budget.

Nevertheless, signing an experienced centre-back and a striker remains a priority for the Red Devils, with Collins emerging as a potential option.

According to a report from talkSPORT, the Red Devils are prioritising ready-made defenders, and Collins fits the profile they are looking for.

The 25-year-old joined Brentford from Wolverhampton Wanderers in the summer of 2023 and has since made 124 appearances for the club, scoring eight goals.

Collins is under contract with Brentford until the summer of 2029, meaning the Bees are likely to demand a sizeable transfer fee.

Furthermore, the Bees are pushing for European qualification this season and may be reluctant to part ways with one of their key players midway through the campaign.

The Red Devils have also been linked with a move for Fulham centre-back Calvin Bassey in January, but they may need to act quickly if they are serious about securing his services.

Bassey recently confirmed that he has been negotiating a fresh contract with the Cottagers, potentially leaving Man Utd at risk of missing out on the defender.

The Red Devils have also been long-term admirers of Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite, although the Toffees are expected to demand a substantial fee for their prized asset.

Pochettino may not have the luxury of spending heavily on a single player and could therefore need to offload some fringe players to free up squad space and generate funds for latest arrivals.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

La Liga side, Sevilla, have reportedly set their sights on a January transfer move for Birmingham City winger, Carlos Vicente, less than a year on from the Spaniard's initial move to St. Andrew's @ Knighthead Park.

That is according to Vamos Mi Sevilla, with the Spanish giants currently sixth in their top-flight, having taken 19 points from 13 matches.

Birmingham endured a mixed 2025/26 Championship campaign, but have shown signs that they can potentially mount a sustained promotion bid this term, with Wednesday night's 2-0 success over Burnley seeing them remain fourth.

Vicente was one of two high-profile signings made by the Second City outfit in January, with his move from Deportivo Alaves coming days after seven-goal forward, August Priske, was recruited from Djurgardens IF.

It hasn't been the smoothest of rides for the 27-year-old at St. Andrew's, and he could be on the move once again if his former boss, Luis Garcia Plaza, sees his transfer wish granted.

Vicente was heavily courted by Blues having shone for Deportivo Alaves under Plaza's management, scoring 17 times and posting 13 assists in 82 appearances for his former club.

Such was their desire to retain the winger's services, it was suggested the Championship side needed to pay £17.3m for his signature, before the initial fee was whittled down to £7m as Vicente penned a three-and-a-half year contract in the West Midlands.

Davies has since utilised the wide man's services on 36 occasions, with Vicente scoring five times and posting two assists, but it has emerged that Plaza is wishing to reunite with his former star at the Ramon Sanchez-Pizjuan Stadium.

Reports state that Vicente also has a desire to return to his home country, and that Sevilla are exploring the possibility of an initial loan swoop, which could be made permanent in the summer, by which time the winger will have 24 months' left on his Birmingham contract.

Vicente made 17 Championship appearances in the second half of last season, with his best form coming in the final weeks of the campaign.

In a run of six successive starts to round off the season, the Spaniard netted his first goals against Ipswich Town and Wrexham, and continued to keep Patrick Roberts out of the starting lineup in the current campaign's early weeks.

Despite goals, again, in back-to-back outings against Norwich City and Derby County in September, a strong run of form from Roberts saw Vicente dropped to the bench, before he made a strong impact in his first start in a month in the victory against Burnley in midweek.

During the encounter, the winger created three chances and set Jay Stansfield free for the club-record signing to provide Priske with his seventh-minute opener.

It remains to be seen what Vicente's immediate future holds considering his impact from the get-go against the Clarets, as well as the sheer number of fixtures Birmingham have to contest in the coming weeks.

What does make such exit discourse particularly interesting, though, is that it has coincided with reports suggesting that Blues are, again, plotting a move for Liel Abada, formerly of Celtic, alongside local and promotion rivals, Wolves.

Blues fans, how do you assess Carlos Vicente's situation at St. Andrew's? Comment below!

Abada is capable of featuring on both flanks, whilst Davies certainly isn't short of options at present through the likes of Vicente, Roberts, Demarai Gray and Liam Millar.

As such, this is an intriguing predicament, especially with the January window notoriously hard for conducting vast amounts of business.

By Saikat Mandal | 25 Nov 2026 14:15.

Bournemouth have slapped a hefty price tag on Eli Junior Kroupi as they maintain that the forward is not for sale in the January transfer window.

The 20-year-old joined the Cherries last summer from Lorient and has made 35 appearances for the club across all competitions, scoring 13 goals.

His impressive form has not gone unnoticed, with several top clubs, including Arsenal, Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, taking a keen interest in signing him.

According to a report from talkSPORT, Bournemouth have no intention of selling their prized asset in the January transfer window.

The Cherries are fifth in the Premier League table and will be chasing a place in the Champions League next season, making them unlikely to part ways with any of their key players midway through the campaign.

They are determined to keep hold of the 20-year-old until at least the summer and have slapped a whopping £100m price tag on his head.

Kroupi is under contract until the summer of 2030 and reportedly favours a move to La Liga champions Barcelona if a transfer materialises in the future.

Arsenal are looking to bolster their attacking options in the January window, with signing a versatile winger a priority for Mikel Arteta.

The Gunners have followed Kroupi's progress closely, but whether they would be willing to spend upwards of £100m on the youngster remains a major question.

Moreover, Arsenal have been monitoring other options and could turn to relatively cheaper alternatives, such as Antonio Nusa.

The north London club have also reportedly joined Real Madrid in the race for an ambitious move for Bayern Munich superstar Michael Olise, although a potential January transfer is out of the question.

In any case, the Gunners will likely have to spend big to secure a top-class winger, and while Kroupi could be an ideal addition, prising him away from Bournemouth in January looks a difficult proposition.

Lincoln City are on the lookout for a newly introduced head coach after they made the decision to part ways with Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw earlier this week. The Imps were thrashed 4-0 by Charlton Athletic on Tuesday night, and have now lost five Championship games on the bounce.

According to recent reports, the search for a new leader is underway, and according to Alan Nixon, one man in the frame is Gavin Strachan. He presently serves as a first-team coach at West Brom, linking up with James Morrison’s staff in the summer following six years under various bosses at Scottish giants Celtic.

According to recent reports, nixon states Strachan was first eyed by Lincoln City a couple of years ago but decided to stay with Celtic. He is happy in his current post at The Hawthorns, but he could be more tempted to take on a significant job at Sincil Bank.

According to recent reports, strachan, son of Scotland and Celtic legend Gordon Strachan, has built a reputation in the coaching world. After retiring in 2011, he took up a role in the academy of former club Peterborough United, first serving as boss of their U18s.

Recent findings suggest that he would then step into Darren Ferguson’s first-team staff as assistant manager, and he ended up following him to Doncaster Rovers and back to Peterborough United again in January 2019. When the opportunity to join the Celtic staff arose though, Strachan couldn’t say no.

According to recent reports, it is in Glasgow that Strachan will have learned from some really established coaches. He was part of the backroom teams of Brendan Rodgers, Ange Postecoglou, Neil Lennon, Martin O’Neill and Wilfried Nancy, and he’s now at a West Brom side who are lauded for just how well-drilled they are under Morrison and co.

Recent findings suggest that strachan’s sole first-team managerial role came at Ilkeston Town in 2015. That lack of experience may worry some Lincoln City fans, but his coaching experience could make him an exciting option.

Strachan’s lack of experience as a head coach or manager will concern some of the Sincil Bank faithful. Lincoln City are in a Championship relegation fight, and an experienced leader could be best for their current predicament.

However, the Imps have not been afraid to roll the dice with appointments in recent times.

Mark Kennedy had mainly worked as an assistant manager or in academy football when he was given the reins, and they gave Michael Skubala his first full-time senior head coach role as well. Then, Cohen and Shaw were promoted in a rare move to name joint bosses.

Appointing someone with strong coaching pedigree but limited experience of being the lead man is a theme at Lincoln City, and swooping for West Brom man Strachan would continue it.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.
  • Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.
  • Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 04:37 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 04:38 EST, 24 November 2026.

Radja Nainggolan has claimed his former team-mate Romelu Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement on Belgian football following his shock retirement from the national team.

Lukaku, 33, unexpectedly announced his retirement from international football following Belgium's Nations League matches against Turkey and Italy earlier this month.

Belgium's all-time record goalscorer had been left on the bench against Italy, while he had not been in the squad three days earlier for the match against Turkey.

Lukaku's shock announcement caught Belgian media by surprise, while his former international team-mate Nainggolan has claimed more news will follow from the star.

Nainggolan, who won 30 caps for the national team between 2009 and 2018, revealed on the Ongefilterd Voetbal podcast he had a one-hour phone call with Lukaku following his decision.

The former Inter Milan and Roma midfielder stated that Lukaku told him: 'You are only allowed to say that a bombshell is about to explode.'.

Romelu Lukaku confirmed his shock retirement from international football earlier this month.

In a recent development, former team-mate Radja Nainggolan claims Lukaku is planning a 'bombshell' statement for Belgian football following a one hour phone call with the star. Source: Ongefilterd Voetbal.

'So something is still coming,' Nainggolan said.

According to recent reports, 'What? I don't know. There were some internal problems between him and a certain person. But I'm not going to say much about that.

It has been revealed that 'Romelu will bring that up himself. He was a bit bitter, though. He was disappointed, frustrated.

'We will hear from him soon what will happen.

'About the real problems that were at play, he will be able to explain that better than I.'.

Lukaku's retirement had marked a stunning reversal of his intends, with the former Chelsea and Manchester United forward having vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament with the Belgium national team.

Describing his international career as a 'great ride', Lukaku had confirmed his international retirement on social media.

'16 years old', his Instagram statement began. 'For 16 years, I gave everything for the national team. I experienced every possible emotion. I played with fantastic teammates for whom I will always be grateful.

Lukaku vowed in January that the 2026 World Cup would not be his last major tournament.

The Belgian forward has fallen down the pecking order and spent a lot of time on the bench.

'I want to thank them all. I also want to thank all the coaches for pushing me and giving me the confidence to help the team. It was a great ride, and I enjoyed every moment.

In a recent development, 'To the Belgian fans, thank you for the support you have given our team. I am proud to have represented my country at four World Cups and three European Championships. I will never forget those moments. I am at peace with my decision to stop here. It was amazing, it was a joy. I am grateful. Thank you.'.

The Belgian veteran accompanied his post with a gallery of photographs from his storied international career, from his debut against Croatia under Dick Advocaat in 2010 to his final chapter wearing the armband.

Lukaku has captained Belgium on a handful of occasions since 2020, alongside the likes of Kevin De Bruyne and Youri Tielemans.

The 33-year-old forward, who became one of the hottest properties in world football after breaking onto the scene at Chelsea, has been a regular fixture in the international set-up for almost two decades.

Spearheading Belgium's golden generation, which included star-studded talents such as De Bruyne, Thibaut Courtois and Eden Hazard, Lukaku chalked up an impressive 135 caps for the international team.

He also retired as Belgium's all-time top scorer on 94 goals, just six shy of a century.

After suffering multiple injury setbacks, he featured at the 2026 World Cup under Rudi Garcia and continued to play a crucial role, scoring three times as a substitute to guide Belgium to the quarter-finals where they were ultimately stopped by eventual champions Spain.

Since Mark van Bommel's appointment in August, following Garcia's departure at the end of his contract, Lukaku has slipped further down the pecking order, with Charles De Ketelaere preferred to lead the line.

During Belgium's resounding 4-1 victory over Italy on Sunday, Lukaku warmed the bench as an unused substitute – and wasn't even in the squad to face Turkey three days before.

Lukaku, pictured with Kevin De Bruyne, was an unused substitute as Belgium beat Italy 4-1.

While Belgium were winning in the second half against the Italians, Lukaku was seen warming up on the sidelines in the hope of featuring for one last time, but unfortunately was not given the opportunity.

VTM NIEUWS anchor Maarten Breckx claimed De Bruyne looked 'concerned' while speaking to Lukaku on the bench, suggesting the former Man City star was unhappy to see his team-mate overlooked.

'When it became clear that he wouldn't be allowed to come on, De Bruyne was talking to him. You could see the concern in his eyes,' he said.

Sources indicate that 'You could tell, especially from Romelu's attitude, that he was dissatisfied and displeased. He had probably counted on getting some minutes...'.

With only Jan Vertonghen and Axel Witsel registering more international caps than Lukaku over their careers, boasting 157 and 140 appearances respectively, Belgium are expected to give the 33-year-old forward a send-off he deserves in the near future.

Witsel, who also called time on his Belgium career this year, was one of the team-mates to celebrate Lukaku's retirement on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that 'Thanks for everything, legend. Thank you, what a journey we've had together,' he wrote.

Columbus Crew vs Inter Miami - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways

  • On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.
  • Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 25 Nov 2026 14:16, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:19.

On Friday, the Columbus Crew can pull off what may become the biggest upset in MLS playoff history and eliminate Inter Miami in game two of that first-round series at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field.

Last weekend the Crew took game one by a 3-0 score, putting them in position to eliminate the reigning champions should they win this upcoming fixture.

Columbus had a lot of momentum heading into the playoffs, and that continued on Saturday as they took advantage of some sloppy Miami defending to take a surprising lead in this series.

Laurent Courtois has seen his side score three or more goals in four of their last five matches versus MLS opposition, while posting a clean sheet in three of those instances, making them an appealing option to choose on the UK betting sites.

The Crew exposed gaps in the Miami squad, scoring on three of their five targeted efforts last weekend and putting the Herons on the ropes heading into game two.

This is only the second time they are up 1-0 since this best-of-three first-round format was introduced, with this team advancing past Atlanta United in three games on the only previous occasion in which they were in this position in 2023.

Only once since their 2015 MLS Cup final defeat versus the Portland Timbers have they lost a post-season match at home, with the Latest York Red Bulls blanking them 1-0 in game one of that opening round series in 2024.

Friday will mark the second time the Crew can eliminate Miami from a major competition in Columbus, after knocking them out of the 2024 Leagues Cup thanks to a 3-2 victory at ScottsMiracle-Gro Field in the round of 16.

For a team boasting so much experience and talent in the biggest club and international competitions, Inter Miami failed to keep their composure in numerous instances last weekend.

Saturday’s defeat was the joint-worst for the club in the post-season, though given everything that transpired, they could be looking much worse heading into this match.

Kily Gonzalez will be relieved to know that Lionel Messi is available, escaping with just a caution in game one after throwing the ball at Gonzalo Tapia, a moment some believed should have warranted a sending off for the Argentine.

Miami played a good portion of that match a man down, and have never won the second game in a best-of-three MLS playoff series.

The Herons have given up a combined six goals in their last two matches versus MLS opposition and have yet to beat an MLS club in a knockout fixture this season.

The reigning league champions have lost four of their five all-time playoff outings away from home, with their only triumph coming at FC Cincinnati in 2025 (4-0).

Columbus Crew Major League Soccer form:.

Columbus Crew form (all competitions):.

Inter Miami Major League Soccer form:.

Due to a cruciate ligament tear, Wessam Abou Ali will not be available for Columbus in game two of this series.

Gonzalo Tapia netted twice in Miami, with Taha Habroune also scoring as Patrick Schulte made three stops for the clean sheet.

On the Miami side, Mateo Silvetti is dealing with a shoulder matter, Tadeo Allende still has a knee problem and Israel Boatwright is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Gonzalo Lujan will be suspended following his red card in game one, while Sergio Reguilon, David Ayala and Cesar Abadia are all questionable with lower-body injuries.

Columbus Crew possible starting lineup:.

Schulte; Farsi, Moreira, Zawadzki, Amundsen; Zaroury, Chambost, Habroune, Rodriguez, Tapia, Mendez.

Inter Miami possible starting lineup:.

St. Clair; Fray, Casemiro, Micael, Falcon; De Paul, Bright, Segovia; Messi, Suarez, Berterame.

While Miami have all they need to come back and win this series, they are far too rigid defensively and give away too many quality scoring opportunities, which is why we believe their season will end much earlier than most would have expected.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City have made it five league wins on the bounce for the first time since 2008 following their 2-1 home win over Millwall, as the likes of Jack McGlynn and Viktor Johansson have joined in with Potters supporters' trend involving George Hirst.

Stoke continue their incredible run of form in the Championship, making it 11 wins, two draws, and one defeat in their 14 league games, after having lost all three of their opening games.

The Potters have emerged as surprise automatic promotion contenders this season, and with West Ham United away on Saturday, face arguably their biggest task yet since this mighty run of form began.

Back-to-back home victories over Birmingham City and Millwall mean they will head to the capital full of confidence, as the goalscorer from those games has drawn attention on social media.

George Hirst joined Stoke in the summer window from Ipswich Town for an initial £6 million, rising to £10 million, and with just one goal in his first 14 Championship games for the club, drew criticism from some supporters.

However, after netting the only goal in Stoke's 1-0 victory over Birmingham and both of the Potters' goals in their 2-1 win over Millwall, the Scottish international has silenced a few doubters, with his goal celebration against Blues not going unnoticed.

Celebrating his goal against Birmingham with Luke Graham, Hirst mimed spreading butter on bread, a nod to his interview whilst with Ipswich, where he scored a late penalty, incidentally against Blues, saying in his post-match interview: "[Scoring the penalty] is what I'm paid to do. It is my bread and butter.".

Now, some Stoke players have seemingly picked up on this, and taken to Instagram to react to his recent brace against Millwall.

Setting up Hirst's first goal against the Lions was American international Jack McGlynn, who has adapted tremendously to English football following his late summer switch from Houston Dynamo.

The midfielder has been a revelation for the Potters, and among their most important players this season, and alongside star shot-stopper Viktor Johansson, has taken to social media to react to Hirst's brace.

With just two simple bread and butter emojis, McGlynn and Johansson know exactly what they're making a nod to, and if Hirst continues to score at the rate he has over the past couple of games, it certainly won't be the last time those pair use those emojis this season.

What do you make of McGlynn and Johansson's nod to Hirst's celebration? Do you think Stoke can continue this run of form? Share your thoughts below!

With Hirst undergoing a slow start to life upon his move to Stoke, he has certainly silenced some of his doubters this week.

Lamine Cisse's injury has afforded the Scot a run of games in the side, though with both Sam Gallagher and Robert Bozenik waiting in the wings, Hirst must ensure he keeps firing at this rate if he wants to keep his place in the side.

There is growing optimism around the Potteries right now that this year could be Stoke's year, and Mark Robins will be hoping Hirst can keep firing them in at this rate to ensure that dream becomes a reality.

Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

💡 Key Takeaways
  • There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago.
  • Sources indicate that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025.
  • If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Sources indicate that everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a major night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” noted Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”.

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

Recent findings suggest that A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA.

It has been revealed that how Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his upcoming territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

In a recent development, quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Industry observers note that iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move unveiled the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

According to recent reports, your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still highlighted great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm.

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

Sources indicate that “I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”.

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS.

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”.

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw.

With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

Sources indicate that “It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the newly introduced Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Recent findings suggest that andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”.

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

In a recent development, ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

It has been revealed that “What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil noted. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”.

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

By Matt Law | 25 Nov 2026 14:30, Last updated: 25 Nov 2026 14:32.

Manchester United are expected to be active during the January transfer window, with the club potentially making three mid-season signings.

The Red Devils right now find themselves down in 19th spot in the Premier League table and facing what would be a stunning relegation from the top flight.

There could also be first-team departures in the winter market, as new head coach Mauricio Pochettino begins to shape the squad.

Here, Sports Mole looks at five players who could potentially leave Old Trafford when the January market opens for business.

Zirkzee was linked with a move away from Man United over the summer, but he was ultimately not allowed to depart due to the fact that the Red Devils were unable to sign a replacement.

Even with Benjamin Sesko out injured, Zirkzee has not started a single match this season, with each of his 11 appearances coming off the bench.

The Netherlands international has scored twice this season, but his overall record for Man United since arriving from Bologna in 2024 is 11 goals in 86 appearances.

It has been a struggle for the 25-year-old in English football, but he is not short of interest, and a return to Serie A in January is seen as a serious possibility at this stage.

Como and Napoli are the latest clubs to be linked with Zirkzee.

The 29-year-old has underperformed in his nine appearances for Man United this season and is not believed to be in the club's long-term aims.

Initially, the defender impressed after arriving from Bayern Munich, and he has now represented the Red Devils on 86 occasions in all competitions.

However, a switch in the January market could be on the cards, especially if Man United are able to boost their options at full-back in the winter window.

Heaven is reportedly open to the idea of leaving Man United during the winter market.

The 20-year-old has made eight appearances for the Red Devils this season, including five outings in the Premier League, but he was an unused substitute against Liverpool in the team's last match, which ended in a 4-0 defeat.

Man United are expected to bring in a new centre-back in January, and Heaven is noted to be concerned over what that would mean for his playing time.

As a result, the Englishman is allegedly open to a winter loan move, while a permanent exit is not being ruled out depending on what offers arrive.

Heaven, who has a contract with Man United until the summer of 2029, has made 32 appearances for the club since arriving from Arsenal in February 2025.

Martinez's contract with Man United is due to expire at the end of the campaign, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a tough season for the Argentine.

A fresh deal for the 28-year-old is seen as highly unlikely given that he has openly criticised Man United chiefs, such as director of football Jason Wilcox, during the 2026-27 season.

Man United will be reluctant to lose the Argentina international on a free transfer, so it is possible that a sale in the January window could occur, depending on the offer.

Martinez has been one of the team's biggest under-performers this season, and it appears that his time at Old Trafford will come to an end at some stage in 2027.

Amass may yet be given the chance to prove himself to fresh Man United head coach Pochettino, but the defender's future looks to be away from Old Trafford.

The 19-year-old was heavily linked with a departure during the summer window, but he stayed at Man United past the deadline and has made two appearances this season, both in the Champions League.

Amass was not in the squad against Liverpool last time out, though, and Luke Shaw's return to fitness has pushed him further down the pecking order.

A number of Championship clubs are believed to be keen on the teenager, who only has a deal with the 20-time English champions until the end of the season.

Published: 05:07 EST, 24 November 2026 | Updated: 05:13 EST, 24 November 2026.

Premier League clubs are bracing themselves for a latest raid of their talent from Saudi Arabia, as the mega-money league considers relaxing spending rules.

Teams in the Saudi Pro League (SPL) are currently only allowed eight foreign players in their 25-man squads but are discussing increasing that number to 14 or even higher.

If the move is approved, it is likely to trigger a flood of cash in the market similar to the massive £765million spree in 2023 that saw the likes of Cristiano Ronaldo, Karim Benzema and N'Golo Kante sign for Public Investment Fund (PIF) teams.

In that 2023 window, almost half of the transfer fees received by Premier League clubs came from the SPL.

In total, 94 players were signed by Pro League clubs and the January transfer window could now follow a similar pattern.

The Saudi spending reached such astronomic levels that it eclipsed every other league in Europe aside from the Premier League.

Cristiano Ronaldo (right) and Angelo, pictured in action for Al Nassr, are among the foreign stars already plying their trade in Saudi Arabia and more will be on their way.

The supposed reason for the proposed rule change is to elevate the standard of existing Saudi players at home by raising the overall level of talent ahead of the country hosting the World Cup in 2034.

But critics argue that the new rules would only force Saudi players out of their domestic league in place of high-profile foreign recruits.

While Premier League clubs are often reluctant to allow talent to leave in January midway through the season, the fees on offer from Saudi can be eye-watering and hard to turn down.

Aston Villa sold Jhon Duran and later Ollie Watkins for a combined £115million to the SPL.

Fulham accepted £50m for Aleksandar Mitrovic, while Wolves banked £47m for Ruben Neves and Liverpool were able to recoup almost £50m for Darwin Nunez.

West Ham were able to cash in on Crysencio Summerville after relegation last term when Al Hilal bought him for £60m.

In a recent development, would Man United consider offers for Bruno Fernandes as his contract winds down? Or will they keep the club captain to help battle relegation?

Suddenly every Premier League club recruitment department will be reassessing their squads and be keeping a close eye on the rule developments in Saudi.

Ollie Watkins moved from Aston Villa to Al Hilal and the Premier League side have recouped huge fees from the SPL in the  past.

Ivan Toney (second from left) and his Al Ahli team-mates celebrate a goal against Al Nassr.

The SPL's decision on whether to allow the increase of foreign players will be clarified before the winter window opens.

The PIF are winding down their investment in golf through LIV having invested more than £3.7billion since 2021 but their operation in football shows no sign of slowing down.

Players weighing up a move to Saudi will perhaps have a more difficult decision than in 2023 over relocating, with conflict still affecting the country.

The Asian Cup was postponed earlier in November following a missile attack from Yemen-based Houthi rebels on Riyadh airport that killed 13 people and injured more than 300.

Security fears and geo-political uncertainty could make footballers think twice before accepting the lucrative contracts on offer in January and beyond.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers have officially confirmed that their side will be backed by a sell-out travelling contingent for the upcoming Lancashire derby against Bolton Wanderers at the Toughsheet Community Stadium.

It has been a campaign of mixed fortunes for Rovers, with the side who many tipped for relegation at the beginning of the campaign right now 12th.

A 1-0 victory against Watford at Vicarage Road on Wednesday night saw Blackburn reach 25 points after 17 games, just three points outside the play-offs.

Such feats come after the news that Tony Mowbray would be stepping back from his role due to health reasons, with Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds currently overseeing matters on the touchline.

And it's fair to say the interim duo will not be short of backing against Steven Schumacher's side on Saturday week.

As the crow flies, there are just 10 miles which separate Ewood Park and the Toughsheet Community Stadium, with this region of the country known for several historic rivalries.

Rovers fans, of course, will not quite have the same feelings of animosity towards the Whites as they displayed against Burnley on November 22nd, but it is one of three eye-catching fixtures from their perspective - the other being against Preston North End.

Bolton, of course, returned to the Championship for the first time in seven years in May, renewing this particular Lancashire rivalry in the process.

Yet, whilst attendances at Ewood, largely due to Blackburn's ownership situation, remain heavily criticised, not many will do the same after Rovers confirmed that over 5,000 supporters will make the short journey for next weekend's early kick-off.

It was confirmed on November 20th that away supporters wanting to purchase a ticket for Blackburn's clash with Bolton could do so on a general sale basis, after those with 4,500 or more points on the club's loyalty scheme were given a two-day headstart.

Even if the journey is straightforward, those in the away end still had to part with a sizeable sum of cash, particularly if they are an adult-paying supporter.

Indeed, tickets in such brackets cost £36, whilst an adult wanting to take one junior supporter with them to the match still had to part with a combined £45 for the two tickets.

However, the aforementioned bundle was only available in the upper tier of the Toughsheet Community Stadium's away allocation.

This may come as little surprise too, as Bolton rank sixth in the Championship when it comes to the average price of a ticket for visiting supporters.

Given their recent four-point haul, Rovers now sit level with five other Championship sides in this particular metric, having taken 10 points from a possible 27 on the road.

Bolton, meanwhile, have failed to make their home ground the fortress it needs to be in order to consolidate, winning just two of their first nine matches at the Toughsheet.

Blackburn will look to pile on the misery in that regard, especially with the recent form displayed by Andri Gudjohnsen, whose father, Eidur, enjoyed two spells with the Whites.

Blackburn fans, will you be attending the away fixture at Bolton Wanderers? Comment below!

While both fanbases will be looking forward to this matchup, the two sides have clashes with Birmingham City and Charlton Athletic to focus on first.
