Enzo Maresca believes streetwise Enzo Fernández will give Manchester City an extra winning edge – as he told his record £125 million signing to forget about the size of the fee.

City made the Argentina midfielder the joint most expensive purchase in Premier League history with their deadline day swoop from Chelsea.

Maresca has opted against naming Fernández among his captains’ leadership group, which features Ruben Dias, Erling Haaland, Marc Guéhi and Gianluigi Donnarumma.

But the Italian – who knows Fernández well from their time together at Stamford Bridge – is confident his fierce competitive instincts will bring an added dimension to his side.

“I don’t know if it’s streetwise but he knows how to win,” Maresca said, who is in line to hand Fernández his debut against Coventry on Saturday. “When you want to compete or win, it’s much more important to have players that already know how to do that than players who have never done it in the past.

According to recent reports, “Enzo is not the only one. This squad has many players who know how to win titles and how to compete and this is what we are looking for.

Industry observers note that “I know Enzo quite well and I know what he can bring to the team. He is a winner, [has] a winner’s mentality and knows how to win [after] the World Cup, Club World Cup [success].

“I just remarked he is a winner and when you belong to the squad and another winning player arrives, they are always happy.

It has been revealed that “I can promise you that in the last four or five days, four or five players from the squad were asking if was coming or not because they wanted him to be with us. It’s very notable that he is with us.”.

Maresca stated he planned to use Fernandez predominantly as a No 6 or No 8 depending on the game. “I see Enzo as a six, a little bit more deep, or [an eight] a little higher arriving in the box,” he said.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of the Saturday afternoon 3pm kick-offs of which we are treated to a rare number this week as Sky and TNT Sports decide to inconvenience only 10 sets of matchgoing supporters rather than the usual 12 or 14. The matches start, purely alphabetically, with unbeaten Brentford hosting Sunderland, Leeds United travelling to Brighton and Hove Albion’s Amex Stadium where they have never won and have come away with only three points in their seven visits, the something’s-got-to-give quasi derby between winless Fulham and pointless Palace, leaders Man City hosting Coventry City for the Sky Blue Cup and Tottenham head to Nottingham Forest in pursuit of their first point to spoil the gaiety of a nation.

According to recent reports, we have Mike McGrath reporting from the Etihad and John Percy at the City Ground and I will endeavour to keep you up to date with developments at the other three grounds via various methods. Forest vs Spurs seems the most consequential of the fixtures, not because either manager is in any danger but because now the window has closed it should give us a clearer picture of how Roberto De Zerbi prepares to marshal his surfeit of wingers into a coherent attack that can break their goalscoring duck and how he proposes to organise a back four that have shipped five goals.

Fulham and Palace have come in for a lot of criticism regarding their recruitment and while I can understand the frustration of the former’s fans for doing so much business with Real Madrid, I think Gonzalo García is a proper player and will shine over the course of the season.

Sources indicate that palace, I think, are paying the price for the January splurge on Brennan Johnson and Jorgen Strand Larsen, not just the inflated fees but the sizeable wages on players who contributed almost nothing. I was at Leeds vs Brentford last week and there was plenty to admire about both sides but fear for Leeds’ so-far commendable resilience at their Amex knacker’s yard and wonder whether Sunderland will be able to live with Brentford’s pace. Manchester City vs Coventry, meanwhile, probably will not give us the Bouaddi-Fernández-Anderson £325m midfield from the start but we might be given a glimpse.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lincoln City are on the hunt for a third managerial figure this calendar year following the midweek decision to part ways with joint-managers, Chris Cohen and Tom Shaw.

The duo led the Imps into their first Championship season since 1961 following Michael Skubala's summer exit to divisional rivals, Bristol City.

Lincoln coasted to last season's League One title, accumulating a staggering 103 points whilst also embarking on a 29-match unbeaten run.

But as the final month of 2026 nears, they are the lowest-placed out of the three sides who earned promotion last term, having taken just 15 points from their first 17 matches.

It remains to be seen which direction is taken by owner, Ron Fowler at the ProAmpac Stadium, but it has emerged that a previous target, now working with another Championship club, has entered the managerial frame.

Lincoln are at the moment outside the relegation zone by three points, with Tuesday's heavy 4-0 defeat to Charlton Athletic at The Valley, coupled with the manner of their side's performance, spelt the end for Cohen and Shaw.

The Imps have won just one of their last six Championship matches, with it now emerging through Alan Nixon - via Patreon - that Gavin Strachan has been listed as a potential candidate.

Strachan, 47, is right now on the coaching staff at West Bromwich Albion under James Morrison, with the Baggies currently within three points of the Championship summit after a 3-1 win at Bolton Wanderers.

Prior to the start of the latest season, the Aberdeen-born man spent six years at Celtic working under the likes of Brendan Rodgers, Ange Postecoglou and Martin O'Neill, with the Hoops winning the last five Scottish Premiership titles on offer.

Following on from Postecoglou's exit to Tottenham Hotspur three years ago, the Australian wished to take Strachan with him to North London, but a deal could not be agreed.

The aforementioned Morrison was appointed as permanent head coach of West Brom this summer after ensuring the Black Country side's survival in difficult circumstances.

As well as retaining Matt Gill, who had been linked with a switch to Leicester City, the former Scotland international midfielder opted to install Strachan and Tony McMahon as part of a fresh-look coaching setup.

Given how highly Strachan is rated on the coaching circuit, Morrison's initial words following the decision read: "I’m also delighted to add Gavin Strachan to the group.

It has been revealed that "Having a fresh pair of eyes from somebody with Gavin’s experience will help us massively. He has worked alongside some top managers, like Martin O’Neill, Ange Postecoglou and Brendan Rodgers, and will no doubt bring fresh ideas with him.".

Prior to his spell with Celtic, Strachan also assisted Darren Ferguson in two spells at Peterborough United, as well as his stint with Doncaster Rovers.

The decision for the Imps to remove Cohen and Shaw from their positions as joint-managers was the sixth managerial change already made in this season's Championship.

Four of those have been made by clubs in a similar region of the table to Lincoln, with Watford, Burnley and Preston North End all replacing Alessio Dionisi, Nicky Hayen and Paul Heckingbottom with Edward Iordanescu, Fabio Celestini and Graham Alexander respectively.

According to recent reports, lincoln fans, would Gavin Strachan be a wise appointment at this particular moment? Comment below!

With the Reds needing to rediscover form, particularly on home turf, in a bid to survive against the odds, supporters will be hoping that the board get their next decision right.

However, it has already been confirmed that no final call will be made ahead of Saturday's daunting task of taking on Wolves, with Shaun Pearson taking interim charge.

Man City's controversial orange kit sparks fan criticism as Premier League restriction emerges

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (842 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.
  • Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.
  • In a recent development, the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 17:29.

Manchester City's decision to wear a striking orange fourth kit during Tuesday's Champions League draw with Napoli has drawn criticism from supporter groups, while Premier League regulations mean the controversial shirt cannot be worn in domestic league matches.

In a recent development, the Citizens abandoned their traditional sky-blue colours for the 2-2 encounter at the Etihad Stadium, unveiling a special-edition strip created by Puma and Italian fashion brand C.P. Manufacturer. The launch formed part of a commercial collaboration, with the collection scheduled to go on sale worldwide on December 1.

The decision proved divisive, particularly as Enzo Maresca's side extended their winless run to five matches. According to Brazilian outlet Trivela, two independent supporter organisations have questioned the timing of the initiative and its apparent prioritisation of commercial interests.

There is also a regulatory complication. City have already registered their three regular kits for the 2026-27 Premier League campaign, meaning their fresh orange design cannot be added to the selection of strips available for league fixtures.

Premier League clubs are permitted to use a maximum of three registered outfield kits during a season, normally comprising their home, away and third-choice designs.

City have already filled those places with their traditional sky-blue home strip, a black-and-yellow away kit and a predominantly white third shirt featuring blue detailing.

Their fresh orange shirt therefore falls outside the competition's permitted selection, regardless of whether the club wishes to use it again.

The restriction is not related to the unusual colour, the shirt's design or its association with C.P. Firm. It follows from the fact that City have introduced an additional strip beyond the three registered for Premier League use.

UEFA's kit regulations operate differently, allowing clubs greater flexibility over the number of approved designs they can wear in European competition.

That explains why City were able to introduce the orange shirt against Napoli and could use it again during selected Champions League fixtures later this season.

The club confirmed the arrangement in an official statement following Tuesday's match, describing the outfit as a special-edition collaboration with Puma and C.P. Manufacturer.

Supporters will have an opportunity to purchase items from the collection at an exclusive pre-sale event at the City Store in Medlock Square on November 30, before the worldwide release the following day.

The FA Cup could also provide another opportunity to wear the shirt, although its use would require the appropriate approval from the Football Association.

Such exceptions are not unprecedented. Arsenal received permission to wear a special white kit in the FA Cup as part of their No More Red initiative, which raises awareness of knife crime and youth violence in London.

The Premier League restriction is only one aspect of the controversy surrounding City's latest release.

According to Trivela, the Citizens Trust, an independent supporter organisation established earlier this year, criticised the decision to introduce the orange shirt and expressed opposition to initiatives perceived as explicitly promoting third-party commercial interests.

Another independent organisation, the 1894 Group, reportedly raised concerns about the club's priorities, arguing that City should be concentrating on strengthening their relationship with supporters during a difficult period.

Those objections are particularly relevant because the new kit made its debut at the Etihad, where City would ordinarily wear their familiar sky-blue colours.

The orange design has no obvious connection to that traditional home identity. However, C.P. Manufacturer has a longstanding association with British football terrace fashion, and its partnership with City dates back to 2024.

The club therefore has a cultural and commercial rationale for the collaboration, even if some supporters remain unconvinced by its appearance on the pitch.

Tuesday's result did little to improve the mood. City were held to a 2-2 draw by Napoli despite a late equaliser from Rayan Cherki, extending a difficult run for Maresca and his players.

The manager is already facing questions about his team's performances ahead of Sunday's Premier League trip to Arsenal, making the timing of a high-profile commercial launch a particularly sensitive matter.

City have previously demonstrated that fourth kits can generate interest without provoking the same debate over their relationship with the club's identity.

Their 2024-25 special-edition shirt, developed with Noel Gallagher, celebrated the 30th anniversary of Oasis's debut album, Definitely Maybe.

The design drew on the Manchester band's history and Gallagher's longstanding support for City. It was worn during Champions League fixtures against Inter Milan and Paris Saint-Germain.

The latest collaboration follows a different approach, reflecting C.P. Organization's influence on football fashion rather than a specific event from the club's own history.

Recent findings suggest that there is no indication that City intend to withdraw the orange kit following the criticism. Their official announcement identifies it as an outfit for selected European fixtures, and the commercial launch remains scheduled for next week.

For supporters attending Premier League matches, however, there will be no repeat of Tuesday's unusual appearance. City's three registered domestic kits will remain the available options, leaving the orange shirt as a feature of their European campaign.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The first South Wales derby between Swansea City and Cardiff City for just short of two years takes place on Sunday, and clarity has been provided regarding the hosts' search for a latest head coach.

Swansea started the Championship campaign in fine fettle, leading the division as recently as October 17th under Vitor Matos, who then made the decision to join RC Strasbourg, much to the bemusement of those in South Wales.

The Portuguese was only installed as Alan Sheehan's replacement 12 months ago, winning 22 of his 47 matches in charge, with the last of those being the late loss at Birmingham City on November 7th.

Within a rather frosty announcement by the Welsh side, it was confirmed that Kris O'Leary, Ashley Williams, Joe Allen and Leon Britton were to lead the 2-2 draw against West Bromwich Albion last weekend, before also overseeing Tuesday's 2-1 loss to league leaders, Middlesbrough.

With ownership duo, Brett Cravatt and Jason Cohen, seeking a swift replacement, clarity has now been provided as to who will lead the Swans for the weekend's grudge match against the Bluebirds.

Despite a recent dip in form, Swansea are narrowly outside the early-season play-off places, and, if results fall their way in the next 72 hours, they could return to the top eight.

The club's current situation has led to intense speculation over who could take the reins, with Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick initially linked, before reports emerged over the potential hire of Rosenborg boss, Freyr Alexandersson.

Alexandersson's current employers are presently fourth in the Norwegian Eliteserien and have three matches to play in a bid to secure European qualification.

Despite the 44-year-old acknowledging such links, it has been revealed by Sky Sports' Anthony Joseph that the quartet of Williams, O'Leary, Britton and Allen will take charge against Cardiff, and, potentially, the three subsequent fixtures as Alexandersson may see out the remainder of the campaign at the Lerkendal Stadion.

Unsurprisingly, the fact Swansea may now have to wait at least two more weeks for full clarity on who takes the long-term reins in the dugout has sparked an immediate reaction.

One of many responses read: "Whilst the derby was always going to be a bit of a push. We can't wait until 13th, that's another 4 games and a significant amount of points on the table and then to ask him to settle over christmas period. It has to be now or never for me.".

Another wrote: "If we have to wait until 13th December, move on.".

"Will be like when we persisted with Sheehan last season, need a upcoming manager in asap," said another Swans fan.

Industry observers note that however, some took a more philosophical outlook, with one comment reading: "The right appointment is the much better option than the quick appointment. You have to laugh.".

Sources indicate that whilst uncertainty on the managerial front could be a hindrance for Swansea, especially with games against Bristol City, Bolton Wanderers and Charlton Athletic on the horizon potentially before a decision is made, in the short-term, the presence of Williams and Co. on the touchline may be a major benefit against Cardiff.

With the quartet boasting over 1,200 appearances for the club, they are aware, more than most, of how much this derby means to the locals, especially having lost the last meeting to a Bluebirds side who were ultimately relegated in rock-bottom to League One.

It also remains to be seen whether an upturn in form lands the Wales assistant a chance of the permanent role, but that will not be on Williams' mind right now.

By Darren Plant | 25 Nov 2026 17:37.

Oliver Glasner has outlined how Nottingham Forest must improve during Friday's Premier League fixture against Chelsea.

However, there is an argument that Xabi Alonso's Blues are suffering from the same complications as their East Midlands hosts.

Forest head into their upcoming game sitting in 17th position in the Premier League table, seven points adrift of their eighth-placed opponents.

While Forest's underlying statistics in the final third have been encouraging, individual mistakes have sometimes cost them.

Speaking at his pre-match press conference, Glasner acknowledged that Forest's players must perform better in many areas of their game.

In a recent development, the Austrian told reporters: "We’ve been talking a lot about running here. You can see we’ve climbed the bottom of the table. We are starting to be in mid-table with all these stats. I think we can see this progression.

"The physical – especially the running stats – are getting more and more competitive. You don’t need to be a heavyweight boxer in our squad. But you need to anticipate. You need to be quick in legs and in mind.".

Industry observers note that when addressing other problems, he added: "We all thought and wished we would have more points. Performances in many games were better than results. We wanted and expected more from us to be honest.

It has been revealed that "We have to accept the reality. I’m no magician. I have no magic dust I can spread. We need to improve our individual mistakes.

"We need to improve our efficiency in attack. Still no goals from set pieces. I think I always talked about stability and consistency. This is what we still have to find and do better.

"To really perform consistently on a high level, we get enough points and we get enough wins. Then you climb the table and this is what we’re looking for.".

After the 4-1 defeat at home to Leeds United, Alonso gave a dismissive answer when a reporter claimed that Chelsea were unable to cope physically against the majority of Premier League teams.

However, it has been clear to supporters that Chelsea possess a team that struggle on that front, with decision-making and in front of goal.

Add in the frequent individual mistakes and you get a similar team to Forest, albeit one that is less physically-imposing.

There is an argument that Chelsea are the perfect opponents for Forest to return to form.

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER and LEWIS BROWNING, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:32 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 10:28 EST, 24 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino suggested the Leny Yoro red card that had such an affect ontheir defeat by Liverpool game was 'unfair' and that their opponents should have been 'punished' too.

Pochettino gave up his job as US national team coach to join United on Wednesday, but any hope of a new manager 'bounce' evaporated after Yoro was sent off inside eight minutes and his team were thrashed 4-0.

It was the joint-heaviest defeat for a latest United manager since Lal Hilditch a century ago, and leaves Pochettino's side second from bottom of the Premier League.

'So painful, so disappointed,' said the Argentine, who blamed the early red card for United's defeat. 'It's not OK to start a game in the Premier League with this situation. The game changed completely after eight minutes. Now we can explain everything, but the damage is done – it's so painful.

According to recent reports, 'It's clear that after eight minutes the initiative was in the bin. Do you think that is easy? Even the best team in the world playing in this situation concedes four goals or maybe more.

'We are not going to lose more than one game how we lost today. I take the responsibility, and we keep pushing.

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino blamed Leny Yoro's red card for his side's defeat by Liverpool.

Yoro (right) was sent off for fouling Alexander Isak inside eight minutes of Sunday's game.

'We feel pain for this defeat, but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger into energy to start to work from tomorrow for the next game.

According to recent reports, 'We are in a situation that this is very complicated. It's difficult, yes, but I think we fight, we made the effort, and I know how they feel now in the dressing-room.

'The players are feeling the pain of the result. I told them to be calm: it was an unfair situation that happened. We need to accept that reality. We need to try to increase our focus, concentration and make better decisions on the field.

'We also need to be critical on ourselves but some situations happened in the game that we are not happy.'.

Pochettino was unhappy that referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro a straight red card for his challenge on Alexander Isak, having taken no action over a similar incident involving Jeremy Jacquet and Bryan Mbeumo in the Liverpool penalty box moments earlier.

'In Leny's case, it wasn't intentional. It was an unusual situation that is normal. Everyone who plays football can feel it,' added the United boss. 'If you review the VAR you can see for sure, he never had the intention to connect with Isak. The ball was going to the goalkeeper.

In a recent development, 'If you look before, in the sixth minute, Jacquet on Mbeumo. If you compare the actions, that was a penalty. We were punished badly and they were not punished, that is the truth.'.

He later added: 'One centre-back made a mistake and wasn't punished and us, we made one mistake and we were punished.'.

Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes agreed their team-mate should not have been sent off.

United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo agreed with Pochettino that it wasn't a red card.

In a recent development, 'No chance,' remarked Mainoo. 'The ball is already with the keeper, and they're both running full speed. What can he do?

'I feel like the game has been taken out of our hands early by a red card that I don't think can be a red card.

Industry observers note that 'It's hard but no-one is going to save us. We have to come together and keep digging, keep fighting, and it will come round.'.

Captain Bruno Fernandes, meanwhile, added: 'I can understand the fall, but it's never a red card, and I think it's too many referees on the pitch and too many on VAR with a long time to see, do it in slow motion, and make a mistake like this which can change the game.'.

Gary Neville, who was left slapping himself in the face in shock live on Sky Sports, was pleased with damage control on, with United conceding four when it looked at one point that it would have been many more.

Former United captain Roy Keane, however, wasn't, and took aim at his ex-side's display.

Recent findings suggest that 'I thought United were desperate,' he stated. 'So bad. Neville's OK with 4-0? Are you telling me they could have done better? 4-0 is not too bad with 10 men? Has anyone ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done.

Roy Keane (pictured), meanwhile, questioned why Gary Neville was pleased with the scoreline.

Recent findings suggest that 'People who played for the club said 4-0 is not too bad? Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish?

Industry observers note that 'Liverpool were excellent but how easy did United make it for them? This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we're talking. We're blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers. When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making?

In a recent development, 'Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone's coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.'.

Middlesbrough dressing room insight reveals how players really feel about Southampton clash

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Middlesbrough midfielder Myles Peart-Harris has noted the Boro squad are "excited" for a "massive game" against Southampton on the South Coast on Friday night.
  • According to recent reports, it's the first meeting between the two sides since the play-off semi-final last season, which Spygate ultimately overshadowed.
  • The games went ahead, and Southampton prevailed in extra time after neither side could be separated in 180 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough midfielder Myles Peart-Harris has noted the Boro squad are "excited" for a "massive game" against Southampton on the South Coast on Friday night.

According to recent reports, it's the first meeting between the two sides since the play-off semi-final last season, which Spygate ultimately overshadowed. Ahead of the first leg, Boro officials caught a Saints analyst illegally spying on their training session.

The games went ahead, and Southampton prevailed in extra time after neither side could be separated in 180 minutes. However, the EFL would then expel Tonda Eckert's side from the play-off final and reinstate Middlesbrough to take on Hull City at Wembley.

Sources indicate that since the Tigers beat Boro in May, the rivalry between both fanbases has been brewing, and was stoked by Eckert being handed just a fine and a suspended sentence by the FA for his role in the operation last month. A week ago, the German was given a fresh contract at St Mary's.

Fans of clubs can often play down the importance of games, or brand something as "their cup final, not ours," when discussing a matchup between two new rivals, but deep down, both Southampton and Middlesbrough fans want to get one over each other on Friday night.

Peart-Harris, who took his chance back in the starting eleven for the first time in two months on Tuesday night with a goal and an assist in the 2-1 win over Swansea City, watched on from home as Spygate played out back in May, given he wasn't at the club.

However, the 24-year-old knows how much the game means on Friday, and is looking forward to being a part of it.

"Everyone was watching it [the spygate developments]," he remarked, per the Northern Echo. "I remember watching the semi-final, and then I think maybe a week later you hear the news about what happened. So now, it's definitely something I’m excited to be a part of.

Industry observers note that "Friday's a massive game. It’s a massive football game before anything else, but the rivalry that we now have makes it even better.".

On how the rest of the team feels heading into the game, a lot of them will be looking to pick up a significant win to almost right the wrongs of the last time they were down at St Mary's in the play-off semi-finals.

Recent findings suggest that "The boys are looking forward to Friday. Hopefully we go down there, and we play our football, we stick to what we know and get a result," he continued.

Sources indicate that "We're ready, and we’re excited. I think we're just more excited about the game of football that's going to actually happen, because we know they like to play football, we like to play football, so I think tactically it's going to be a great game for everyone to watch.

"Our aim will be to go down and just get a win.".

As Peart-Harris mentioned, first and foremost, though, Friday night will be a great chance for two of the best sides in the division to go head-to-head.

Kim Hellberg and Tonda Eckert are widely regarded as two of the brightest up-and-coming coaches in the game, and in the past year since they both took over at their respective clubs, the brand of football being played has been fascinating to watch.

This season, Boro have picked up 35 points, while Southampton have collected 32, albeit the four-point deduction handed to them in the wake of the Spygate charges by the EFL means that they sit on 28, seven points adrift of their visitors on Friday.

Who do you think comes out on top on Friday? Let us know in the comments.

The Teessiders have a tough task on their hands, with Eckert's side utterly dominant at home this season. The only side to have come away with any points from St Mary's through eight games were Bolton Wanderers, who needed to rely on a good defensive display to grind out a 0-0 draw.

According to recent reports, it'll be intriguing to see if Boro set up any differently to help combat an unstoppable force on their home patch. Either way, these two teams, and both managers, are destined for the Premier League, and it'll be fun to see them lock horns for the first time this season.

Ultimately, this brooding rivalry is more to do with those in the stands, and perhaps the two coaches in the dugouts, too, even if both have since buried the hatchet after the incident back in May.

The Southampton players who were there to play out the semi-final in the play-offs last season likely weren't to know what Eckert and co were doing to help prepare them for games, and aren't really to blame. Taylor Harwood-Bellis, who was the pantomime villain, mocking Aidan Morris with a spy celebration after Shea Charles' winner, is no longer at the club.

According to recent reports, they will be emotionally charged by the atmosphere inside St Mary's on Friday, though, which will have a little more of an edge to it. As mentioned earlier, both sets of fans may pretend not to care, but they do, deep down.

A red-hot atmosphere and two good footballing sides should create a wonderful cocktail of Championship football, and if both teams are up for it, it could go down as one of the games of the season already.

By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.

Alanyaspor will be looking to halt their alarming slide down the Turkish Super Lig standings when they welcome Konyaspor to GAIN Park on Friday evening.

The hosts sit 14th in the table with 12 points from 12 matches, while the visitors occupy 15th place with eight points and will be hoping to close the gap after suffering three consecutive league defeats.

Alanyaspor have endured a difficult period in recent weeks, losing five consecutive league matches and leaving themselves increasingly vulnerable to being dragged into the relegation battle.

The Thunders began that sequence with a 3-0 defeat away to Fenerbahce before suffering a 2-1 home loss against Kocaelispor six days later, and their struggles continued when they travelled to face Genclerbirligi, suffering a humiliating 5-0 defeat, which was followed by a 2-0 home loss to Trabzonspor.

Those results led to Joao Pereira leaving by mutual agreement, with Ugur Ucar subsequently appointed, but the new manager was unable to bring about an immediate improvement as Alanyaspor were beaten 2-1 at Kasimpasa in his first game in charge.

They have now lost five Super Lig matches in a row and are without a win in their last six, drawing one, leaving Ucar with plenty to address as his side attempt to rediscover the form that helped them collect points earlier in the campaign.

Their recent performances have also been particularly disappointing defensively, having conceded 12 goals across their last five league matches, making them the worst-performing side in the division over that period.

The 4-1 victory over 12 Bingolspor in the Turkish Cup is the only positive result the Thunders have recorded during that spell, and just their second home win across all competitions, having won only their opening home league game, drawn two and lost two, leaving them without a league victory on home soil in their last four attempts.

However, Alanyaspor have enjoyed the better of recent meetings between the sides, remaining unbeaten in their last six competitive encounters with Konyaspor while winning each of the last five.

Konyaspor, meanwhile, have also struggled to maintain consistency this season and are four points behind the hosts, having collected just two wins, two draws and eight defeats from their opening 12 league matches.

Ilhan Palut's side have also lost their last three league games, suffering a heavy 4-0 home defeat against Galatasaray before losing 1-0 away to Samsunspor and then 4-2 against Besiktas in their latest outing.

Aside from their poor record in this fixture, the Anatolian Eagles have another concern heading into Friday's encounter, having collected just one point from five away matches this season.

In fact, Konyaspor have failed to score in their last four away matches, losing three of those games by a 1-0 scoreline, with a goalless draw against Kasimpasa coming between those defeats.

The Anatolian side have also failed to win on their last three visits to Alanyaspor, losing the previous two by 2-1 scorelines after drawing 2-2 on their earlier trip.

Alanyaspor will be without Fidan Aliti, who is suspended for Friday's encounter, leaving Ucar with a defensive selection concern ahead of the match.

Fatih Aksoy and Paolo Fernandes are also carrying fitness concerns, with both players reported as injury doubts, although their availability could be assessed closer to kick-off.

Ruan and Hwang Ui-jo are expected to feature in attack, while Ianis Hagi and Gaïus Makouta could provide creativity from midfield as Alanyaspor look to improve their scoring record.

Konyaspor will be without Adil Demirbag, who is recovering from an injury and is expected to remain sidelined, while Chidozie Awaziem is also a doubt.

Palut could therefore retain much of the side that started against Besiktas, with Enis Destan and Jackson Muleka expected to provide the attacking threat, while Deniz Turuc and Jean-Luc Dompe could play important roles in supporting the forwards.

Alanyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Victor; Hadergjonaj, Lima, Ozyurt, Ozdemir; Makouta, Maestro; Kaya, Hagi, Ruan; Hwang Ui-jo.

Konyaspor possible starting lineup:.

Gungordu; Oguz, Yazgili, Bosluk, Masuaku; Turuc, Toth, Ibrahimoglu, Dompe; Destan, Muleka.

Alanyaspor are struggling to produce consistent performances at both ends of the pitch, but their home advantage could prove notable against a Konyaspor side that has also experienced a difficult run of results.

However, the home side’s defensive problems should give the away side’s opportunities to find the net, and with both teams desperate to avoid another defeat, we expect a closely contested encounter to finish level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This is how champions are supposed to play and, although the Arsenal home support have not seen a team defend their place at the apex of English league football for two decades, they knew it when they saw it.

It has been revealed that the chase was on for Mikel Arteta’s team within two minutes when Morgan Rogers, the man who might have moved to Arsenal this summer, put his newly introduced club Chelsea in the lead. So unfolded a thrilling 100 minutes of Premier League competition. Arsenal were the better team in terms of ambition and attack even if one could not discount Chelsea until the very last moment.

Industry observers note that others might have crumbled. That Chelsea did not will give Xabi Alonso hope for a team that did not feature the injured Moisés Caicedo and is now without the departed Enzo Fernández. Yet he will also recognise that his childhood friend from San Sebastián in the other dugout has created a side that treated the game, and their place in it, with an urgency that looks different. The first two minutes might have been ragged for Arsenal but after that they did not let the game happen to them.

It has been revealed that morgan Rogers fires Chelsea in front inside TWO minutes! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/ca8cqnT2Wm.

According to recent reports, instead, Arteta’s players drove this contest, and the sequence of chances that came and went was dizzying at times. Their best players scored the two goals. First Kai Havertz, who now has three in four games this season, and then the captain Martin Ødegaard who dispatched what would be the winner.

"A spear through the heart of Chelsea!" Martin Odegaard puts Arsenal in front at the Emirates 🎯 pic.twitter.com/5deEQykjck.

Ødegaard looked like the veteran of a title-winning season, and a deep run in the World Cup – an accomplished, shrewd performer in a midfield that was fought over ferociously all afternoon.

As for the game’s defining moment – it would be hard to overlook the feint from Havertz for the winning goal. It deceived the Chelsea players around him and created the channel for Christos Tzolis’s cross to reach Ødegaard. His goal was a close copy, in style and personnel, of the one he scored against Manchester City in the Community Shield but it was crowned by Havertz’s bluff. He shaped to take the ball and let it run under his foot at the last moment.

Industry observers note that this was Chelsea’s first defeat in three – leaving only Arsenal and City with nine points from their first three games – although the seven goals conceded is the standout. For all the jet fuel in their attack they keep conceding. This was a much more exacting test than Fulham and Brighton previously, but even so. Alonso has introduced his preferred back three, often a back five, and it is a work in progress.

Arsenal have set the standard in that regard and they were uncompromising again. They did not replicate the errors that led to the Rogers goal and they pushed the limits at all times. Gabriel Magalhães kicked Emi Martínez in the head competing for a ball in the Chelsea area. Myles Lewis-Skelly went after João Pedro. Ben White and Roméo Lavia saw things differently in the first half. This Arsenal team does not shy away from those confrontations in the way their predecessors often did.

Sources indicate that in fact, it was notable just how furiously Rogers reacted to Declan Rice when the two England team-mates converged as the Chelsea man charged off to join a late counter-attack. The bad feeling lingered even after the game when Rogers seemed unwilling to forgive. Rice had applied the minimum contact and the maximum cynicism to stop Rogers while the attention of referee Chris Kavanagh was elsewhere.

"He's FUMING Morgan Rogers!" 😳 pic.twitter.com/FciivEedvh.

All that ringcraft was one thing, but it should be mentioned that Arsenal were excellent in setting an attacking tempo that will be hell for any team to live with – especially at the Emirates. Havertz is now Arteta’s centre-forward of choice in the absence of a big summer acquisition. Viktor Gyökeres made a late substitute’s appearance – his first minutes of the season. The hierarchy is clear: last season’s great goalscoring hope is now back-up.

It has been revealed that “Exceptional” was how Arteta described his team’s response to the early Rogers goal. They had twice failed to clear the ball in their own area when first Maxence Lacroix and then Jorrel Hato created the chance. Rogers’s right foot half-volley was not struck on the full, but it was placed perfectly inside the post with the necessary bounce and skip to mean David Raya never got behind it.

Arteta’s squad runs deep enough that in the closing stages he could relieve his midfield with two Spanish World Cup-winning substitutes – Martín Zubimendi and Mikel Merino. Then there was Noni Madueke on for Bukayo Saka, understudy and first-choice for club and country. This was not Saka’s day in the way it has been in the past, although a very promising shot of his was stopped by Martinez in the first half.

In the pounding that Chelsea took after they went into the lead, Riccardo Calafiori had an equaliser within minutes that was disallowed by VAR on an offside call. The left-back was the third in sequence to try to force the ball over the line from a Rice free-kick. Calafiori was successful, but the second of his team-mates to try, Ezri Konsa, had been offside when he connected.

Recent findings suggest that for the equaliser it was Havertz, accelerating cautiously at first and then full-on with his left foot from the right-side. Ødegaard was well-placed to prevent Lacroix getting close but in truth the challenge never had the force required. Havertz’s shot was not totally convincing but then neither was Martinez’s attempt to save it – every bit as uncertain as Raya for the Chelsea goal.

Industry observers note that A precise finish from Kai Havertz and Arsenal are level! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/DqL1MEX4zN.

Industry observers note that chelsea had profited from the quick ball out to their right where Calafiori was often out of position in the left-back slot and Pedro Neto could cut in on his left foot. That seemed to be the sacrifice that Arteta was prepared to make in keeping the hammer on Chelsea. If Neto had not struck the post in one such escape in time added on at the end of the first half it might have been different.

According to recent reports, ødegaard struck what would be the winner early in the first half, and although Chelsea fizzed enough in the later stages it always felt as though it was Arsenal’s game. Raya came into his own in the 89th minute when Estêvão, a substitute, cut in from the right and hit a fierce shot that the goalkeeper pushed over. It was close in some ways – and in others not at all.

In a recent development, “It hurts. It hurts because a defeat has to hurt. It has been a very intense game with different moments for everything. We had chances to equalise. In the first half as well a couple of chances. Never happy if you lose.

“After we scored, there were 15-20 minutes where we had to defend too much and we were struggling a bit to get control. We then had better spells with the ball. Overall, it was a very tight, very intense game. We could do better with the second goal to conceded too early. The guys gave everything, tried everything. It has to hurt.

Sources indicate that “It is about preparing the best possible way to compete the best possible way. You need to control the overloads on the right side. It is part of the game to have these actions. We continue. It is game three and this is going to be a long, long ride.”.

"That's not sustainable" Daniel Sturridge reflects Chelsea's performance after the 2-1 defeat to Arsenal 💭 pic.twitter.com/3EMx88QLA0.

"He's not the goalkeeper that won the World Cup" 🏆Jamie Carragher states Emi Martinez is not as quick or sharp as he once was 🧤 pic.twitter.com/SOp4XhoYIr.

Industry observers note that “I think the worrying thing for everybody else already is that [William] Saliba, who is genuinely world-class arguably, probably the best centre-back in world football, has not played a minute of football so far this season. And it does not look like anyone can score against them.

“There is a massive gulf between both teams; their XIs and the squads. It will take Chelsea a while to get to that level, if they can get there. But I thought Arsenal were fantastic today. We do not normally see Arsenal in these games, end-to-end, because they very rarely go behind. They are so strong defensively they do not need to get involved in those games.

“They still did not look like they were going to give too much away, even though they were bombing forwards and putting so many bodies in the opposition box.”.

Recent findings suggest that “It was a massive game with a tough opponent. It was really hard for us; we got there in the end. Our mentality is to keep fighting. Conceding early was not ideal but we reacted really well. We played well in the second half and got our reward. We highlighted our quality today. The result reflected that.”.

On his relationship with Kai Havertz:.

“He is a really smart player and moves so well. He takes defenders attention. When he makes the run and I come from behind I am always free. It was a brilliant goal.”.

Sources indicate that “We knew Arsenal were the better team and they have proven that in this game. The question before today was, how close are Chelsea? And [Xabi] Alonso will be proud of what he has seen. There are obviously improvements to be made, but they gave it a right good go. A lot of very good things and they will be frustrated and disappointed, but they may potentially look back on this game as a good moment rather than as bad as it may feel right now.”.

Industry observers note that it is a relationship that Arteta has previously described as “deeper than just a friendship”. It started with skateboards and sand, as they made the daily journey to the beach to play tennis and football, and continued into their adult lives. When Alonso was playing for Liverpool and Arteta for Everton, there was a time when they both had flats on the fourth floor of the same building in the Albert Dock.

It is extraordinary that these two individuals – born just a few months apart – now find themselves in positions of such significance in English football. But it is not a coincidence. Throughout their lives, they have driven each other forward.

“This kid, he was maybe even crazier than me about football,” Alonso once said of Arteta and their shared childhood. “He was a little bit younger than me and my friends – just a few months maybe. But you know how you always push your ‘little friends’ at that age? Well, we tried, but he was a competitive monster.”.

Joao Pedro always seemed to cause problems for Arsenal’s defence when he played against them during his time at Brighton, and he has a flexibility and versatility that would have been perfect for Arteta’s system. Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta insists Arsenal are “better equipped” for success this season, despite falling short in their attempts to add a top-class attacker. Arsenal have allowed four forward players to leave this summer and brought in one, Greece winger Christos Tzolis.

Industry observers note that the departures of Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, Gabriel Jesus and Ethan Nwaneri (on loan) have raised concerns among supporters that the champions lack firepower. Moves for Morgan Rogers, Vinicius Junior and Julian Alvarez did not come to fruition. Arteta, though, feels Arsenal are stronger now than at the end of last season following a summer in which they added midfielder Bruno Guimarães and defender Ezri Konsa.

According to recent reports, “We are better equipped,” mentioned Arteta, who faces Rogers and close friend Xabi Alonso. “We have more players available than the start of last season. We have increased the quality and we have increased the leadership, which is very important.”.

Asked specifically about the attack, he added: “Yeah, but that’s another question. We have to prove in that particular position whether we are better or not. Let’s see. We need to play. I don’t like to make assumptions.

Sources indicate that “It’s not just the responsibility of those players, it’s the team and the dynamic. We have multiple options to play there with different profiles. It’s human nature. When you talk to people and you ask: ‘Ok, what is on your bucket list?’ Sometimes we forget the reverse bucket list, which are the things you already have that are incredible. It’s very key to value what we have, what we have created together. The ambition is great, but [don’t] lose perspective to what we already have which is amazing.”.

Two sides with 100% records meet in a London derby in north London as defending champions Arsenal host Chelsea at the Emirates. Arsenal have wins over Coventry and Aston Villa to their name whilst Chelsea have beaten Fulham and Brighton.

Arsenal could make it three wins from three to start the season, a feat they have only achieved once in the last 21 seasons. They have lost just one of their last 29 Premier League London derbies. Mikel Arteta comes up against his childhood friend Xabi Alonso today.

“Really happy for him [Alonso],” Arteta said. “It is incredible because obviously we have the history we have together, the same with Andoni [Iraola]. To be facing each other at such a level and with the responsibility we have managing some of the top clubs in the country is a really beautiful thing to experience. Now it will be tougher to meet because of the schedule we both have but that friendship will go for many years. We shared some great moments but now it is the competition and when you face each other, you know what happens.”.

Chelsea were involved in late drama on transfer deadline day. They were on the verge of signing midfielder Lamine Camara from Monaco only to see that deal fall through at the last minute. After being linked with a move away throughout the summer, Chelsea did in the end sell Enzo Fernandez to Manchester City for a joint Premier League transfer record fee of £125m.

Sources indicate that “In football, many things happen and you need to be prepared for everything,” Chelsea boss Alonso stated. “With Enzo, we have had conversations, but always with respect for what he has done for the club. It has been great, we are thankful, but it is time to move forward. We take all the decisions together. We are responsible for them, we work together with every decision, significant and small.

Sources indicate that “We knew that, ultimately, the last goal is to have the best for the team, the best for the squad, the best for daily work here. We want to build a good spirit, a good team, and we have always taken decisions thinking we want to reach that. We have the squad we have. We have a lot of big personalities, players with a lot of quality in all the different positions, different lines and now we are ready to go.”.

Arsenal won this fixture 2-1 last season, with William Saliba and Jurrien Timber earning Mikel Arteta’s side three points on their way to the title. Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches against Chelsea.

Team news from the Emirates to follow shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jeff Stelling had backed QPR for relegation from the Championship, as they now chase promotion to the Premier League.
  • It has been a positive campaign so far for the R’s, who are in the play-off places, and they have played some good football under Julien Stephan.
  • This has come on the back of an inconsistent first season under the Frenchman, which ultimately saw QPR finish 15th.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jeff Stelling had backed QPR for relegation from the Championship, as they now chase promotion to the Premier League.

It has been a positive campaign so far for the R’s, who are in the play-off places, and they have played some good football under Julien Stephan.

This has come on the back of an inconsistent first season under the Frenchman, which ultimately saw QPR finish 15th.

In a recent development, therefore, it was hard to predict exactly how QPR would perform this season. Whilst there had been some encouraging signs under Stephan, the Londoners lost eight of their last 13 games in the previous season, which included four straight defeats at the end.

So, there was frustration among the supporters that they couldn’t build on a decent start, and many wondered whether they would take that negative momentum into the 2026/27 season.

And, it clearly influenced Stelling, with the TalkSPORT presenter and former Soccer Saturday host predicting relegation for QPR back in August.

It should be noted that Stelling made it clear he had no problem with the R’s, and he even admitted he would ‘offend’ their fans, and that he ‘hopes’ he would be wrong.

Pleasingly for QPR, it looks like he will be, as Stephan’s side are 16 points clear of the bottom three, and they’re just seven points behind leaders Middlesbrough, so they are certainly focusing on the other end of the table right now.

We all make calls that are way off, and that looks to be the case with Stelling and QPR here.

The Championship is notoriously difficult, and that unpredictability is why it’s such an enthralling league, even if it was a bold shout to say the R’s could be relegated.

Nevertheless, they are having a good season so far, and most fans would’ve snapped your hand off to be in the play-offs right now, particularly with the way the team are playing.

That’s probably the most encouraging aspect of everything for the R’s, as it doesn’t feel like they’re in a false position, and, if anything, they maybe deserve to be higher in the table.

All credit for that goes to Stephan, as he has built a stylish, attacking side that has proven they can compete with the best teams in this league.

So, the focus for QPR will be to make Stelling’s prediction look even worse come May, when they will hope to be back in the Premier League.

That may seem like a long shot when you consider the resources of the clubs they are competing against, but, as outlined above, they are a very good Championship team right now.

In a recent development, will QPR win promotion this season? Let us know in the comments below.

There will be concerns about how sustainable a promotion push is, and the lack of depth in certain areas, such as the final third, could be their undoing.

Therefore, January will be crucial, and the R’s may need reinforcements if they are to make this season a truly memorable one.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.
  • Caykur Rizespor will look to extend their recent improvement when they welcome Kasimpasa to the Caykur Didi Stadium on Friday.
  • The hosts are 10th in the Turkish Super Lig table with 17 points from 12 matches, while the Apaches sit fifth on 23 points, with the visitors arriving in Rize in a stronger position after an impressive run of results.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joshua Cole | 25 Nov 2026 18:32.

Caykur Rizespor will look to extend their recent improvement when they welcome Kasimpasa to the Caykur Didi Stadium on Friday.

The hosts are 10th in the Turkish Super Lig table with 17 points from 12 matches, while the Apaches sit fifth on 23 points, with the visitors arriving in Rize in a stronger position after an impressive run of results.

Rizespor head into Friday's fixture with renewed confidence after collecting back-to-back victories against Erzurumspor and Amedspor, having endured a difficult spell during October.

Their latest success was a 2-0 away win over Amed SK, with Ali Sowe scoring both goals to take his league tally to six, as the Black Sea Sparrowhawk became the first side to claim a league victory at Diyarbakir Stadium this season.

That result followed a 2-1 home victory over Erzurumspor, while they had previously played out a goalless draw away to Kocaelispor.

However, the Black Sea side's recent recovery should be considered alongside the problems they experienced earlier in the campaign, having suffered defeats against Corum, Fenerbahce and Trabzonspor before beginning their current three-game unbeaten run.

They will look to build on that form against a side they beat 3-0 in their last meeting, while they can also take encouragement from recording their first home victory of the season after losing their opening four league games at Caykur Didi Stadium.

Kasimpasa, meanwhile, have put together an impressive sequence of results and arrive in Rize having won four of their last five league matches, with their only dropped points during that period coming in a 2-2 draw against Besiktas.

The visitors followed that draw with a 2-0 victory away to Gaziantep before recording a 2-1 win over Alanyaspor in their most recent league outing, with Adrian Benedyczak scoring twice, including a late penalty to secure all three points.

The Apaches are now unbeaten in their last six matches across all competitions, winning five of those games, including a 3-1 victory over Corluspor in the Turkish Cup.

The visitors will head into this fixture with added confidence from their recent record at this ground, having avoided defeat in their last three away games against Rizespor, drawing once and winning the previous two.

Kasimpasa Turkish Super Lig form:.

Kasimpasa form (all competitions):.

Rizespor are expected to be without Khusniddin Alikulov, who is recovering from a knee injury, and Can Bozdogan, while Valentin Mihaila is a doubt with a calf problem.

Sowe has scored four goals in his last two league appearances and will be looking to make the difference again as he leads the line.

Kasimpasa have several potential absentees of their own, with Kamil Corekci, Godfried Frimpong and Mortadha Ben Ouanes among the players carrying injury concerns.

Ayberk Karapo is suspended, while the availability of Fousseni Diabate and Kevin Mouanga is also uncertain.

The update lands during a busy early market for Xabi Alonso’s incoming rebuild.

The Guardian’s latest transfer round-up states that Chelsea like both West Ham forwards, while an earlier report noted Chelsea and Manchester United had tracked Summerville.

Summerville, meanwhile, fits the younger, explosive one-v-one profile that would sit neatly inside Alonso’s longer-term wing plan.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the final whistle, the first song the stadium DJ played was Spirit of the Blues and how those relieved Evertonians lapped it up after a week of angst.

In a recent development, their team had been on the precipice of a defeat that would have exacerbated all the frustrations that bubbled away following the chaotic conclusion to the transfer window. Indeed, it was 10 seconds over the allotted five minutes of added time when the ball fell to Ainsley Maitland-Niles.

It had been three years since the former Arsenal full-back had played in the Premier League – his last goal in England was on October 30, 2019, in an EFL Cup tie with Liverpool at Anfield that ended 5-5 – and he would not have joined Everton if their attempt to sign Kenny Tete from Fulham had not failed.

But here he was 30 yards from goal, with no need to break his stride as Manchester United’s backtracking defenders presented him with an invitation to shoot. So that’s what he did. With one perfectly timed swish of his right foot, an unlikely hero transformed the mood of a club.

"That is something SPECIAL!"Ainsley Maitland-Niles earns a draw for Everton on his debut with an unbelievable 96th minute strike! 🤯 pic.twitter.com/HNdx9PxrUP.

“Brilliant technique,” remarked David Moyes, Everton’s manager, who had only introduced Maitland-Niles in the 77th minute after James Garner had succumbed to cramp and could run no more. “We are still getting to know Ainsley but that was a brilliant goal.”.

According to recent reports, only those with the coldest hearts would begrudge Everton this point, which was especially hard-earned given they had conceded an 88th-minute header to Benjamin Sesko. But there is no chance a disbelieving Michael Carrick will feel that way.

It has been revealed that benajmin Sesko puts Manchester United back in front! 👊 pic.twitter.com/MF3A9LyaY8.

Recent findings suggest that united should, really, have won this game comfortably. Everton were there to be exploited and when Bryan Mbuemo put them ahead early in the second half, they should have powered away into the distance. Everton’s effort was good but they were in danger of losing hope.

Yet, incredibly, United gave Everton two helping hands. They had not been in a position to assist last Tuesday evening, when phone calls from Merseyside to Old Trafford to take Joshua Zirkzee on loan were met with rejection. But the second half display more than made up for that.

“We’re bitterly disappointed,” stated Carrick, who was one step removed from having steam puffing from his ears. “All the work that went into putting us in that position at different stages to then come away like that… it’s not a great feeling. It feels like a defeat. It’s a bit of a cliché to say.”.

But clichés are true. First United were passive when Tyrique George crashed in a brilliant right-footed drive in the 83rd minute and then, after Sesko profited from Jordan Pickford’s weak hands, they were passive again in allowing Everton to build the move that ended up with Maitland-Niles’ howitzer.

How had it come to this? It was beautiful bedlam, the kind of joy that only football delivers, but for long periods it felt like it was an opportunity for United. There was anticipation that Everton’s fans would create a furnace but there was also the fear it would be dispiritingly quiet.

Had this fixture been at Goodison Park, with its steep stands, tight confines and acoustics that split your ears, United would have been aware of the siege mentality as soon as their bus rolled up outside the stadium but their upcoming sparkling home is rather more hospitable.

It has been revealed that this is no criticism of the home crowd – it is anything but. Why should it always fall to them to bail out the failings of those in charge when those in charge, specifically the executives and recruitment department, have given them scant reason to have hope?

The route to victory for United, then, was relatively straightforward: for all Everton’s initial huff and puff, it always appeared that it would be a case of the away team repeating the simple things, retaining their concentration and waiting for a breakthrough.

According to recent reports, it could have come as early as the eighth minute. Luke Shaw’s deep cross to the back post picked out Mbuemo, whose cushioned header invited Bruno Fernandes to take aim but the Portuguese’s volley clipped the crossbar with Pickford stranded.

United dominated and Marcus Rashford was central to it all, a scampering presence down the left who gave Merlin Röhl, playing as an auxiliary right-back, all kinds of problems. The only thing missing from his opening 45 minutes was a goal.

In a recent development, when Mbuemo scored so early after the break, it felt as if this was going to be one puncture too many for Everton to withstand and the anticipation was United would get the job done. In all fairness to Moyes, however, he was not in the mood to accept excuses.

According to recent reports, his substitutions were all positive, with Jack Grealish changing the mood and Hayden Hackney providing dynamism. But it was the former Middlesbrough man who drove forward to give George, whose loan move from Chelsea was made permanent in June, the opportunity to smash an 83rd-minute bullet past Senne Lammens.

"That was unanswerable!"What a way for Tyrique George to open his account for Everton! 🔵 pic.twitter.com/c0HPRjWUia.

Sources indicate that “I told the players there would be no excuses and the players all agreed,” Moyes noted. “They have hugely bought into it. And, you know, sometimes when you have [fewer] players it means everybody has to be ready. Sometimes when you have a small squad you have to find a way of making it work.”.

They did just that. Pickford should have saved the header from Sesko that looked as though it had given United the lift, but Everton, with their manager belligerent and their fans sensing all was not lost, had other ideas. The noise they generated as Maitland-Niles’s goal went in was unique to this stadium.

As Moyes celebrated, shaking his fists and revelling in the positive turn of events, Carrick put his hand across his face and shook his head repeatedly. All the while, Everton’s fans sang I guess that’s why they call it the Blues. United’s head coach certainly had them. Everton, simply, had relief.

In a recent development, 2 - For just the second time in the last 50 years, Manchester United have conceded 2+ goals in each of their first three games of a league season, along with 2020-21.Leaky. pic.twitter.com/B2Dk6Ioxkq.

It felt like a win. The crowd was with us, we fight to the end and that’s how you get that type of result.

It has been revealed that it’s amazing. Everyone wants to start like that and fortunately I did. I put my foot through it and it ended up in the top corner which I’m happy about.

I came here to work hard. It’s a team full of hard workers and I fit right in. I’m going to show I can pull my weight and give as much as everyone else, if not a little bit more.

Even I have a lump in my throat to see him do that after his original move to Everton in August 2021 was stymied by a late change of heart by Mikel Arteta. Don’t normally approve of badge kissers but he has waited such a long time for that and must have thought his chance had gone.

Sources indicate that just time to kick off before the whistle goes. Probably a fair result and that goal from Maitland-Niles was good enough to win a game never mind save it.

George finds himself in a near identical spot from which he scored and tries again with a thumping shot that flies into the side-netting via Lammens’ finger tips. He was offside on this occasion, though.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Stoke City have continued their incredible run of form under Mark Robins with a 2-1 home victory over Millwall on Wednesday night to send them joint top of the Championship alongside Middlesbrough.

Everything is rosy right now in the Potteries for Stoke, who can’t stop winning at the moment, with their most recent victory over Millwall extending their winning streak to five games on the spin.

The last time the Potters were on such a run was back in 2008 with Tony Pulis at the helm; they would go on to win promotion to the Premier League that year, as now with Robins in the dugout, Stoke supporters will be hoping history can repeat itself.

However, there is still a long way to go, and the club cannot afford to rest on their laurels or become complacent anytime soon, as one former fan favourite has revealed the two things they must do to secure a Premier League return this season.

Although Stoke sit in the automatic promotion places in the Championship right now, a mere ten points separates them from 12th place; as for how good things have been, it only takes a poor couple of results to go back to reality.

Former goalkeeper and fan favourite Asmir Begovic, speaking to The Sentinel, has now revealed the two things the Potters must do this year to fire their way back to the top flight.

Begovic said: "It's not easy to get out of the Championship, but it's good to see them having a positive start. Listen, there's still a long way to go. Now we're getting into the meat and bones of the season going into the Christmas period, and it's really notable to try to continue being consistent.

According to recent reports, "They've obviously made some really good signings as well, Ethan Galbraith has been absolutely outstanding, a great signing. So for some of the things that have gone wrong, you've got to give the board and Jon Walters credit for strengthening the squad.

"Now it's about keeping that consistency, maybe adding the latter piece or two in January given their resources and positioning. The fact that the play-offs have also extended has given a lot of teams a lot more hope as well.".

Do you agree with Begovic's take on the matter? What do you think Stoke must do to secure promotion? Share your thoughts below!

Begovic, 39, has had an exceptional career in professional football, beginning his career with Portsmouth before spells with Macclesfield, Bournemouth, Yeovil Town, Stoke, Chelsea, Qarabağ, AC Milan, Everton, Queen’s Park Rangers, and Leicester City.

It would be with the Potters where he would play the most games in his career, making 173 appearances across all competitions in North Staffordshire, having joined the club from Portsmouth in January 2010 for around £3.25 million, and eventually being sold to Chelsea for around £8 million.

In a recent development, speaking to The Sentinel, the Bosnian has been full of praise for current Stoke number one and Sweden international Viktor Johansson, saying: "I think he certainly does have Premier League potential. I think you can see now he's being very selective with his next move. I think he wants to continue to play.

"I'm sure he would have had opportunities to go in as a number two at times, but I think the fact that he wants to play and be number one for club and country shows a lot about his character and his mentality. I think he definitely has the capabilities and talent to play in the Premier League.".

Johansson penned a fresh four-year deal at the bet365 Stadium over the summer, having initially joined the club from Rotherham United in the summer of 2024 for just over £1 million, and has been exceptional ever since.

Certainly, Johansson will be hoping to play Premier League football one day, and at this rate, there is no reason it can’t be with Stoke.

Robins has been in similar positions before, but to date, has not quite gotten over the line, at least not in the Championship, falling short with Coventry City and suffering a major dip in form last year with Stoke.

The 56-year-old will be well aware of the position he is in, what he has to do, and how to do it, but should still listen to the advice the former Bosnian international has laid out before him.

The January window presents Stoke with an opportunity to add one or two fresh bodies to the mix, and if they are to get over the line, those additions could be pivotal in their year, as transfer plans must be in place ahead of the coming months, whilst remaining consistent has to be the priority for now.

Latest Update: Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's camp issue joint statement after contract pressure controversy

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.
  • Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.
  • The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 25 Nov 2026 18:40.

Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala's representatives have issued a joint statement following talks aimed at easing tensions over the midfielder's health and contract, just days after the club was accused of putting public pressure on the Germany international.

The 23-year-old's future has become a sensitive subject at the Allianz Arena, with senior Bayern figures openly questioning whether he can regain his previous level following a difficult period of medical problems.

Those remarks prompted criticism from global players' union FIFPRO, which accused the German champions of pursuing a "coordinated strategy" to pressure Musiala and his representatives ahead of possible contract discussions.

However, Bayern have now taken a significant step towards addressing the controversy. Following a meeting on Tuesday, November 24, the club and Musiala's agency, 11WINS, published a statement emphasising their shared commitment to the player's recovery and clarifying an notable detail about his medical history.

The announcement comes less than a week after Musiala returned to action during Bayern's 1-1 Bundesliga draw with Cologne, having missed almost two months through injury.

In a statement published on their official website on Wednesday, Bayern confirmed that discussions with Musiala's management had taken place the previous day.

"A constructive meeting took place between FC Bayern Munich and the management of Jamal Musiala yesterday (Tuesday)," the club announced.

According to recent reports, "For both sides, the player's health comes above everything else. Musiala is being given full support on his road back.".

The statement also addressed speculation surrounding the timing of the midfielder's neurological symptoms, which became public earlier this year.

Bayern and 11WINS confirmed that Musiala underwent his first examination for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they initially appeared.

Crucially, that examination took place more than two months after the Germany international signed his contract extension until June 2030 on February 14, 2025.

The clarification establishes that the medical concerns arose after the agreement was completed, addressing speculation about whether the condition had been known when the lucrative deal was negotiated.

Bayern added that the examination had been conducted in consultation with the club and its medical department.

The statement concluded by confirming that the two parties had agreed to maintain contact and continue discussions "in a spirit of partnership and trust".

According to Sky Germany, Musiala's representatives Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschaffl attended Tuesday's meeting with Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen, president Herbert Hainer and sporting director Max Eberl.

Notably, honorary president Uli Hoeness and supervisory board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, whose earlier comments contributed to the controversy, were not present.

The joint statement represents a change in tone following several weeks of increasingly public discussion about Musiala's situation.

Hoeness, Dreesen and Rummenigge had all raised questions about the potential consequences if the attacking midfielder failed to recover his previous form.

Rummenigge was particularly outspoken after Friday's draw with Cologne, suggesting that Bayern might eventually have to reconsider the financial terms of Musiala's contract if his performances did not justify the sums involved.

Those comments attracted criticism from FIFPRO, which argued that the club's senior figures were placing unnecessary pressure on a player dealing with significant health concerns.

The union called for contractual matters to be handled privately and emphasised the importance of respecting agreements already signed by both parties.

Further questions emerged following a report by Suddeutsche Zeitung about a meeting between Hoeness and Musiala's agent during the summer.

According to the German newspaper, Hoeness believed there had been a verbal understanding that the midfielder's contract could be revisited if his condition prevented him from returning to his former level.

Musiala's representatives reportedly interpreted that discussion differently, understanding only that the parties could hold further talks if the player's situation failed to improve.

Tuesday's meeting did not produce any declared agreement to alter the contract.

Indeed, Eberl told Sky Germany that salary matters had not been discussed, with the immediate focus instead placed on supporting Musiala's return.

The sporting director also expressed confidence that the midfielder could regain his best form, stressing the need to give him time without additional pressure.

Musiala's contract remains valid until 2030, and neither Bayern nor his representatives have unveiled any changes to its terms.

The joint statement therefore provides an notable clarification about the circumstances surrounding the original agreement, while leaving the longer-term contractual questions unresolved.

💡 Key Takeaways
